Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds This recycling truck is awesome. It takes two AA batteries (included for demonstration purposes only—meaning they may have to be replaced using a Phillips screwdriver shortly after use). The biggest difficulty I had is in removing this truck from the box because it arrives in the ON condition and started working immediately as I was trying to unpack it. That was a bit annoying.

The on / off button is located underneath the truck under the cab. There are two levels of sound and lights to choose from when turning on.

Once the truck is on, the button in the center of the CAB turns on the ignition sounds and the lights come on.

The lights also come on when pressing down on the tires and moving forward and backward. When moving backward, the backup warning sounds activate.

The recycling truck container opens in back and can store Legos or other small toys. It also tilts back to the rear.

All the sounds of dumping, loading, and idling are realistic. Pressing down on the horns on either side of the cab also generates realistic sounds.

The recycling bucket has a slot that allows for placement into the hitch. Once in place, move the lever handle down to dump (or pretend dump) what is in the pail. The pail can also be stored in the top of the truck’s container.

The instructions are useless as it only talks about the batteries. Therefore, it is important to pay attention to the pictures on the box or read the description on Amazon to learn how to fully operate this vehicle. Another option is to learn via trial and error.

To me this is an extremely impressive toy for a reasonable price of $29.99.
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Easy-Bake Ultimate Oven Baking Star Edition When i was a kid, i had one of these.  My mom tells the story that I would pull it out to bake and she was like...Oh gosh, there she goes again.  Then i would run up to her, handing her my homemade cakes and she would eat them with a smile and love on her face but thinking "i hope these things are safe to eat and i wish she woudl put that thing away" !  I always loved to bake and so does my mom.  We are scratch bakers and I actually make things for parties etc.  I have a love of baking so when I had a chance to review this, I jumped !  My daughter is 8 and I had her in the kitchen with me since she was a baby and she loves to bake.  She does love this easy bake oven. The mixes that come with it are good but i made my own for her.  We love to experiment together.  It's easy enough, plug it in, let it heat up, mix up your recipe, slide it in then out !  The mixes that come with it are good.  You can find better ones on the internet.  My daughter and I enjoy baking together and this is like a new project for her.  She tries new recipes and when they work, it's a sense of accomplishment.  Plus is bonding mom and daughter time.  The only thing i didn't like is that there is no timer or clock.  Baking does require some kind of clock or timer.  It would be nice if a timer was on this thing because it would totally be the responsibility of the "baker" to hear the timer go off, then go get the item and let it cool.  Otherwise this is a great toy, machine or whatever you want to call it.  It's totally safe too...no worries.

text_fidelity_a:
Imhotep Builder of Egypt | Family Board Game by Kosmos | 2-4 Players | Ages 10+ | Toy of The Year Finalist | Parents Choice Gold Award Winner | Toy Insider Top Holiday Toy | Spiel Des Jahres-Nominated This is just a first-time playing review, which I'll update as we continue to play. But at this point it wouldn't surprise me if the score gets bumped up to a five.

Components: high quality. They seem quite well made, durable, and are beautiful looking.

Set up: Set up is pretty easy and quick despite the number of materials (we played with three)

Gameplay: Deceptively simple. Your goal is to build structures using blocks which you quarry then place on a boat then sail to one of four places then unload them, with various points scored at the ends of rounds and the game depending on what you achieved. It is, as mentioned, deceptively simple because though you only have a few options, the other players of course get to do their own thing, which often involves blocking your thing. So that ship you were planning to load up with that particular stone you needed? Somebody just decided to sail it away. Those stone you loaded on that ship to build a pyramid? Somebody docked it instead at the obelisk area. So you need to work around what your opponents are doing, try to anticipate what they're going to do, as well as try to block them as well. It's fun, frustrating, stimulating, engaging, and did I mention fun?

We really enjoyed playing it even with the usual slow-down issues of playing a game for the first time. Even with those first game issues, the game was finished in under an hour and I would imagine you could get through it in 30 minutes regularly. An additional plus is that although the game will play differently lots of times obviously with all the variations on situations, the game itself comes with a "B" side (in other words, its own variant)

I'll update as we get more games under our hat, but right now Imhotep seems like a winner
text_fidelity_b: Imhotep Builder of Egypt | Family Board Game by Kosmos | 2-4 Players | Ages 10+ | Toy of The Year Finalist | Parents Choice Gold Award Winner | Toy Insider Top Holiday Toy | Spiel Des Jahres-Nominated

text_fidelity_a:
WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums My boys young boys have been rockhounds ever since we moved to Eastern Oregon three years ago. We thought we'd add the the thrill and enjoyment by getting them a tumbler to further explore the joys of rock hunting. There's a certain thrill of putting in raw stones that you think are "pretty", only to see their true beauty one they are polished.

We already have a single barrel WireJewelry tumbler and love it so much that we decided to grab this one to expand our capability. (There are LOTS of rocks here).

As before, assembly and setup was easy. Allowing one to have six total pounds of capacity is amazing. The heavy duty motor doesn't seem to be strained at all, even under full load, so it should last years. The barrel construction is very sturdy and we have never had even a minor leak. By design, they are very well sealed. While the noise level is not bad, I find it best to do my rock tumbling in the garage. The same hum in your house for weeks on end might just get to you.

This company is great for packaging kits, not only for the tumbling media, but for rocks as well. The media kids come numbered and labeled, so the process is super easy to follow. Tumbling is not a quick hobby... each batch can take weeks. Personally, I think that's part of the fun.

If you are thinking of getting into the hobby, I definitely recommend products from WireJewelry, I have yet to be disappointed in their products. Enjoy the treasure hunt!
text_fidelity_b: WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums

text_fidelity_a: Rowood 3D Puzzles for Adults, DIY Wooden Mechanical Model Kit for Teens Kids Age 14+,Educational Toy Home Decoration & Birthday Gift - Solar System I actually nabbed this as a birthday gift for our 11 year old, so he won't be 12 until September, but in spirit of being able to leave a review, I did unbox so that I could inspect the wood, take a gander at the instructions (I am fairly mechanically inclined) and to just get an overall look of the quality of the kit and how well it is laid out for people to assemble.  It gave me a good idea about what frustration level this might be standing at, and from what I could tell, this should be challenging but not to the point of getting super frustrating, more challenging in a good way than in a negative way.  I really like the way they were able to integrate the steam punk feel with the solar system.  We are huge fans of Lego and this seems like this is going to be very similar with step-by-step assembly.  If you have ever put together a 3D rendering of something then you already know what I mean.  Last year, we built the Hogwarts 3D Castle, and while it is labelled a puzzle, it really isn't.  There's nothing "puzzling" about it at all since every direction is very detailed and every piece labelled.  I can also say that this would probably not be a good fit for anyone under 10 unless the child happens to be very focus oriented and has tons of patience.  I feel like once he see's this he is going to want to break into it immediately and start assembly.  He loves building just about anything.  Very impressed with this set and glad I grabbed it.  Hope this review is helpful!

Unsolved Case Files: Cold Case Murder Mystery Game: Who Murdered Harmony Ashcroft? | Can You Solve The Crime? The only reason this isn't a 5-star review is the racist casting in the mystery that had nothing to do with the story.

A friend gave this to me knowing my love for true crime. I've always wanted to try the Hunt a Killer boxes, but was always put off by the price.

No spoiler review:
- The case file includes newspaper clippings, evidence files, interview transcripts, photos, and more. Your first puzzle is to prove the innocence of Bones, the only non-white person in the game who was a homeless drunk that was wrongfully accused and jailed for the crime. (Obviously, racism is very much a problem with our justice system in real life. However, depicting that in a fictional puzzle game? We'll never solve this problem if we continue to portray that happening. Furthermore, there was NO STORY REASON WHATSOEVER for it.)
- You select your answers to the puzzles on their website, and if you're right you can open the first seal additional evidence envelope. I was worried the answer selection would spoil the real answers, but we didn't have to worry about that at all.
- We ended up becoming so invested in the case, after a couple hours in we decided to sleep on it and solve the first puzzle the following day. We couldn't stop talking about it.
- Once you play it once, you can't play it again. However, you don't have to mark any of the evidence so you can easily just put everything back in the envelope and give it to a friend. For the price as well, that's a lot better than most true crime puzzle games that are WAY more expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Unsolved Case Files: Cold Case Murder Mystery Game: Who Murdered Harmony Ashcroft? | Can You Solve The Crime?

Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab Fisher-Price Imaginext toys in general are great toys. Durable, bright colored plastic that often take after popular shows and movies such as Batman and Superman, Power Rangers, or in this case, Jurassic World. These toys have allowed my son's imagination to run wild and be creative as he plays for many hours with these. We often play together, but for the most part he's very happy to play with these on his own for hours at a time. I probably purchased my first Imaginext toy about 3 years ago, Batman and his Batcycle. It has held up to the test of time and a very rough preschooler. My son is now 6 with multiple sets.

Jurassic World has been all the rage in my house this summer because little boys love dinosaurs and that is certainly true of mine! So, take his love for Imaginext toys and mix that with his love for dinos and it's the perfect mashup! The only caveat is that on Amazon I have found the prices to vary greatly from in stores. Toys R Us (R.I.P.) was a great source for Imaginext because they always had the best and lowest price on these. They also had more selections. So, I would caution anyone to first look around Target or Walmart first. I once bought Batgirl and her Batcopter for $30 on Amazon and it was in Toys R Us for $15. I regularly see Imaginext toys in Target selling for $5-10 cheaper than on Amazon.

With the Fisher Price Imaginext Jurassic World Research Lab you get one T-Rex, one scientist, one harpoon, and one claw. There is a "decontamination" chamber for the scientist to get clean to study his subject. Simply turn the powerpad and the blue decontamination spiral gets the scientist ready. There is a powerpad to open and close the cage for the T-Rex. But watch out! The T-Rex might get loose! the lab is not that big. It's smaller than all of the Batcaves I've ever purchased. It's no bigger than any of the Paw Patrol sets I've purchased as well. So, it's east to tuck it away in a corner. All of the pieces, including the T-Rex, we've placed in a plastic show box for organization and storage. Overall, it's a fun play-set that provides hours of entertainment and keeps kids away from screens!

Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles [[VIDEOID:886df78722d87a8bdca79a9702180ce2]] This set is awesome!! There are a couple things to note about it that could be potential downsides/issues, if not prepared for-- but otherwise, everything is great! Below I will group the main points and for the 3 potential issues I'll mark it with this symbol:🔴 to hopefully make it easier to read through!

•We received all pieces included, and boxing, in great condition.

•1 car is included

•The quality of materials are true to Hot Wheels- great and sturdy plastic.

•It's a fairly easy set-up. My 9 year old put it together on her own by reading through the instructions step-by-step. It took around 30 minutes, may have been quicker but she often took short pauses, though she didn't need any help.

•There are about 3 different configurations you can do with this set. The video I posted shows each of these.

•Can connect to other Hot Wheels tracks and sets. (Including the colossal crash set that can be seen some in the background of the video I posted)

•Does not require batteries

•There are no levers that need to be reset for cars to go through the loops- my daughter has other loop sets that have those.

•You can set it up so that the launcher connects and starts at any of the loops. For example- you can connect the launcher to just the middle loop and the smallest. You can also try to launch it opposite- starting at the smallest loop and ending with the largest.

•You don't have to use the jumping ramps…you can have the cars finish the loops on a flat track.

🔴 One of the potential issues is the launcher- maybe it's just our launcher, or how we use it, but it can be a bit tricky to hit it with the right amount of pressure. Too hard and it knocks it off track. Too soft and it won't go around the loop. Sometimes it can take many tries and others it works right away. We have a few other types of launchers-- the long white one that is shown in the video I posted is the one she prefers to use since it seems to work better. Not everyone will have extra launchers, though. My daughter usually has no problem with trying multiple times with the one included in the set but I figured it's worth noting that it may not be a perfect launch each time.

🔴 The other possible issue are the cars used with it. You'll likely want at least a handful of different types of cars on hand, just in case. The one included does work pretty good. My daughter has a decent sized collection of cars and there a quite a few that often don't make it through the biggest loop. This could either be the car itself that doesn't work well or could also be an issue of the launcher (as just mentioned above). Some of her cars struggle on the biggest loop with the launcher provided- but when connected to the "stronger" launcher, they do great. And there's a few that still just don't make it. This could be an issue if this were very first set for a kiddo and if they have only 1 or 2 cars…just something to keep in mind if considering purchasing this set, you may want to consider also purchasing a handful of cars so that they can get the most use from it.

🔴 When you have it set-up as the Daredevil Jump or Gravity Drop, it sort of seems like the track isn't long enough since the cars shoot further past the cup a lot. So we added extra tracks (which aren't included in this set) and it helped a lot…the cars land in the cup more times than not. At the very end of the video I posted, you can see how we added an extra track to the Daredevil Jump set-up.

All-in-all: We love it! It keeps my 9 year old busy-- even if she doesn't connect it to her other tracks. She likes trying to get the cars in the cup and thinks that the triple loop feature is awesome.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles

text_fidelity_a: Educational Insights Panda Rollers I work in a high school special ed classroom. The students are considered to be moderate-intellect. I took this game in to play with some of them. The game can be played with 2, 3 or 4 players. Each player gets a set of 12 "eye" cards. There are two cards of each eye color, but one is a left side of the face and the other is the right side. You have to physically pick up the panda board to shake the dice. At first I thought it was like the old classic game Trouble where you press on the dome to get the dice to move, but that's not how it works. After the dice are rolled, you find the two cards in your pile the match what shows up on the panda board. It took one of my students a while before she started "getting" that the left/ride side mattered, but my other student picked up on it fairly quickly. I ended up with a set of cards, too, and I would position it correctly and model it for the one student to copy. The first person to have the correct eye match, wins a tile. We ended up playing three full games. Both kids liked it a lot. Although they are in high school, it was very appropriate for their academic levels. There's no reading, so we weren't slowed down by that. I would definitely recommend this to other special ed teachers or people with preschoolers.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Panda Rollers

You see they have to view an app, which shows a speedometer. They need to keep the needle at a certain speed. Speedometer graphics is broken down into 2 colors, blue and red. If you go to the red, chances are good your car will fly off the tracks. How do you control the speed? By pumping the booster. The faster you pump, the needle will move towards the red. So you need to time yourself and not pump too slow, or too fast to keep the needle in the blue at all times. My kids seem to think it's fun, so that's all that matters. But if you're an adult or an older child, I think you might get bored. Just pumping and watching the car go round and round. All the hardware is top notch. We first used the [[ASIN:B00IVFCD0Q Monster High Monster Maker]] with an eight year old who guided me through each step. I had already downloaded the software for using on my computer, had installed the included AA batteries, and connected the printer cable. His approach was very different than mine because he wanted to print his design on all the legs, then the arms, then the heads. I wanted to do each of the three dolls as a single being. By inserting the pens which actually can be used to draw freehand, the design is drawn directly onto the doll parts and if you don't like the outcome or grow tired of it, they are erasable. My only complaint about this kit is that two wig caps are included and a single rooted wig whereas the rooted wigs are far superior. The shoes are pretty cute and the dresses are very simple. When I have time, I'll put together some more of the little dresses with fabric scraps.

Keeping all the small parts together is well contained with this set and the [[ASIN:B00LOR4Z3Q Monster High Monster Maker Primary Extension Pack]] is an affordable addition. Because the ink is fairly light when applied to the dolls, there has not been residual color remaining after we've used the eraser to clean them up for refreshed designs. This is a very smart "toy" that is capable of entertaining small groups of children as well as a single designer. Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary [[VIDEOID:e1253051a67b2634f9e78ac021248ab6]] I will be the first person to admit that I purchased these because I always wanted Sea Monkeys as a kid but for some reason I never got them.

The video was shot on day 5 after I put the eggs in. There are quite a few little guys swimming around it the water and they are doing fantastic. I used spring water in their tank, kept my hands and fingers OUT of the tank and placed them in a sunny window during the day and I don't move the tank around much at all. I also aerate them for about 20 seconds every other day with a small air pump and stone that is made for fishbowls, the smallest one you can find.

Mine hatched the day after I put the eggs in.

When the kit arrived, I rinsed it out with the spring water after taking everything out of it. Then I filled it to the fill line with spring water, put the lid on it and let it sit for 24 hours.

The next day, I poured the water purifier in. I didn't stir it, I didn't mess with it at all. I poured the pack in and then put the lid back on the tank.

Next day I aerated the water then poured in the eggs. Again, no stirring or anything. I left it alone, put the lid back on and walked away.

The next day, low and behold I had teeny tiny babies swimming around.

Fed them on the 5th day after they hatched, which was a few hours before I took that video footage.

I'll update again when they are larger but so far I'm really getting a kick out of this. It would appear that the secret is less is more, spring water, don't move the tank around and a lot of patience.
text_fidelity_b: Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary

The printing on his face and chest is a lighter pink than it appears on the box.

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size This is a really great idea for a children's bank and the top part, the counter, works really well. Unfortunately, there are a number of things here that made it not really work for my family. At least not at this time.

First, with little children in the house, the top buttons get pressed accidentally or on purpose when they are not supposed to and so the count has not been correct for that reason. I almost would've preferred some other method of managing bills and kept this as a coin counter only so that you have the immediate feedback putting something in, seeing the number change, and knowing that it's accurate. This would not be an issue in households only with bigger kids who can control themselves from pushing buttons inappropriately, but definitely made it not workable in my house during these years.

Next, I really hoped that the cool top would have threads so that they could fit on a mason jar of any size, so while the little ones are tiny they can have a little chart, and as they grow older they can have a large jar, but unfortunately it does not work with any size mason jar – the sizing, the threads, and the lip that hangs over are all totally different.

Lastly, and this is my main issue, the cheap, foggy, and unattractive plastic container that holds all of the money is so lightweight and is angled weird so that if there are primarily bills with only a few coins in there, the whole thing gets really top-heavy and wants to tip over. My son primarily gets money through finding change on the ground and through getting dollars or 20s on his birthday or Christmas. So there are a few coins in there, sure, but mostly single bills sent from afar through the mail. Had they made the top interchangeable with Mason jars, this would have been an issue because I just would put the whole thing on nice glass mason jar, probably one of those colored blue, purple, or green ones that they've come out with in recent years. Alas, you're really stuck with just the plastic container that the lid fits on. This limits how long anybody would want to use something like this, because I think most teenagers have slightly better taste than to want some cheap plastic thing of a single specific size sitting in their bedroom.

That said, for a very specific age range and if you don't have smaller children around the house, this could work really well and be a very fun way of having kids learn about saving and making it rewarding.
text_fidelity_b: Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size

Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll, Blonde Baby Alive is an iconic doll. She was one of the first dolls that not only took a bottle, but also ate food, mixed and served to her from premade packets. She has been available in many different versions, each with the same eat/drink concept with a slightly different variation. My Baby All Gone is one of the latest Baby Alive dolls and she will easily keep your little one serving, feeding, changing, and burping her baby for hours.

What sets this Baby Alive doll apart from most of the others in the series is her ability to say so many different things. She still takes a bottle, eats food, pees, and poops just like the other Baby Alive dolls, but for a more realistic twist, she makes periodic statements from her wee little mouth. She will say that she wants to cuddle, that she just went pee, and so on. Her baby- ish voice and cute sayings will appeal strongly to young girls still going through their mommy phase.

My girls are both in their early years of elementary school, but they still like dolls and they like Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll just as much if not more than the others in the series, of which they have quite a few dolls. What they like best is the feature that sets this doll apart: The sayings, mentioned above. They like that she says so many different things- more than 30 sayings in all- because it makes her seem more real. I agree that the multitude of sayings is a vast improvement on other dolls that, while they might speak, say only three or four different things. My girls like playing the role of mommy, changing diapers, giving Baby Alive a nap, and everything else that goes with being a mom.

The one disadvantage of this Baby Alive doll is the same disadvantage with the others- you have to constantly purchase refill packs. Trust me, the few packs of food and the small number of diapers will not last long at all! In a matter of a day or two out of the package, your girls will be asking for replacement food and diapers. We have had this doll in our household for only about 10 days and have already ordered a refill pack.

Little girls often like to play the role of a mommy and Baby Alive is one of the best dolls for interactive mommy play. My girls like her very much and I like that they are happy. The cost of the refill packs can add up, so try to improvise when you can or create your own cloth diapers that can be washed and reused. Then watch as the young girl in your household practices her mommy role with a doll that, while not alive, is about as close as you can get to the real thing.
text_fidelity_b: Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll, Blonde

I got this mainly for the metal chess pieces. I see listings on Amazon for the metal pieces alone, and they will start around $45 without a board. I thought surely those "pieces only" sets must be of higher quality than the metal pieces that are bundled with a board, so I weighed all the pieces in this set to compare. It’s a decent set up it lacks some fit and finish that would make it better.

Included in the set is the Mancala board and a plastic bag with multiple colored stones. There is also a concise rulebook on how to play one variant of the game - overall, a decent starter set.

There are several things about this set that make it less than ideal. The most serious problem is the board which has multiple issues. First, it feels unfinished with several very rough spots that are actually visibly rough. This doesn’t make the game unplayable but it does take away. My board is not routed properly and it looks like the design was routed by hand and wasn’t cleaned up properly with wood shavings wedged in the grooves. The reservoirs are shallow and it is easy to spill the stones while playing.

The stones are another matter. There are enough stones to play. However, there are no extras at all and if one or more are lost the game cannot be played correctly without replacements. And, there’s no container beyond a cheap plastic zipper bag for the stones; a cup with a snap-on lid, or a cloth pouch, would be so much better.

This is a playable and functional set, lacking in finishing touches that differentiate it from a good one.

Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games I'm a wolf lover as well as a game nerd and couldn't pass this one up! It is absolutely beautiful out of the box. I'm impressed they kept it to a $50 price point with the level of detail here, I've seen similar games priced closer to $80!

I haven't had a chance to play yet because I need to get folks together but I did watch a video playthrough about the rules after reading the guide so that I'd be prepared. They are complex but once I watched the video it made a lot more sense. It's definitely tactic-heavy in that you need to change strategy based on what your opponent is doing or what phase of the moon it is on. I love many of the creative points in the design, and I love a game with a very clear endpoint because I hate games that go on forever! 75 minutes is perfect for a game night.

I especially love the design of the wolf cards. They are extremely clear where the tiles and meeples go etc. It's not only attractive but it also includes reminder text which is really helpful for absent-minded players like myself. I love how the rules for your items level up as you get more pieces on the board.

My favorite part about games like this is that it's possible to lose a battle here and there and not feel discouraged halfway through. Since a lot of scoring can happen later, it keeps players invested until the end. This generation of games is so different from the ones before!

My only complaint is that with a game like this it is so easy to lose a meeple because they are so small and so many. This can make it hard to trust strangers with at board-game meetups.

Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players This is a very cute concept and something out-of-the-ordinary for a board game! The object of the game is to make it out with the least amount of goo on your shoe. This is represented by actual pieces of putty that you place on the board and squish with your pawn as you land on a square (thus sticking the goo to your, erm, shoe).
My kids really enjoyed it, but I can't help feeling like there are some design flaws that could have been prevented. For example, the spinner needs to be deconstructed to put away in the box. The way the board folds (see picture), the crease is over the spinner area, and with the bars on the spinner (which I like, as it looks like a playground toy) won't fit, which means you have to totally take that apart and rebuilt it each time. On that note, it isn't much of a spinner at all, but just a wheel. There is no clicker or arrow that sticks out to slow it down as it spins... it basically spins until momentum from your push wears out, sort of like spinning a top. It takes a while to finally stop on its own, which makes the game feel like it is moving slowly. I was very tempted to just stop it manually a few times, but that might bring up the possibility of cheating.
Meanwhile, I wish the goo had more colors, or at least colors that matched the shoes in the game. I can say on the positive note, the goo is very kid friendly!
My daughter lost one of the colors and it turns out she was SITTING on it and it was all stuck in her dress. I suddenly had flashbacks of when silly putty got stuck on her clothing and bed and we had to toss them both because it never came off... but this stuff comes off! It easily rolls into balls with your fingers and comes right off clothing in the process. So, definitely some extra points for that! I just wish the game board and spinner were designed a little better, that would make it a lot more fun to play (and put away!).
text_fidelity_b: Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players

It comes with 5 black mannequins, fabrics, sticky jewels, ribbons, needle and thread, and instructions. However, I assumed that you could create a real dress that a Barbie could wear, but you can't - it's just to create a "draft" dress for the mannequin.

You get a bunch of assorted fabric pieces that you're supposed to drape and then insert into the back of the mannequin, where there's a slot. It doesn't come with velcro or metal clasps to hold the back of the dresses together. Then you decorate the mannequin with the ribbons, sticky jewels, etc., and then display it.

If you want to create a full 3D dress for Barbie to wear, you have to sew clasps onto the back - which are NOT included in the set. So you have to pay extra for that. I guess the kit is designed for small children who aren't skilled enough yet to sew buttons or clasps on back of a dress - which is how real dresses are made, not tucked into a slit. Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset Littlest Pet Shop Fairy Fun Roller Coaster Set is a girl's toy featuring the Littlest Pet Shop characters. It is a colorful, cute toy that offers action without the need to purchase batteries. The operation is mechanical so kids can play as long as they want without the worry of batteries dying out.

This toy is nice for many reasons and besides the lack of batteries, the toy offers some simple operation and continuous action. All your girl has to do is press the lever, which moves the stairs upward and slowly transfers the small figures and their vehicles to the top of the slide where they glide around and wind up back at the base of the stairs. If you continue to press the lever, it will gradually pick up the next Littlest Pet Shop figure and send it up the stairs to the top of the slide where it will, once again, make its way around the slide to the base of the stairs.

My girls like this toy and both they and I find it to our liking. If I had to find some type of fault, it would be the tendency for the small vehicles to sometimes get out of place when they reach the base of the stairs. I haven't witnessed any problems with the vehicles gliding smoothly down the slide- the only problem I notice is that the little vehicles will sometimes get out of place at the stairs, requiring some manual assistance to re- position them. This is most likely to happen if kids get carried away and move the lever too quickly. Keep the speed at a moderate to slow rate, and there shouldn't be any problem.

Mechanical toys are nice and even though the Fairly Fun Roller Coaster Set has little or no educational value, it is still a nice toy for girls in the target age group. It is cute, colorful, and provides hours of simple amusement without the need to purchase batteries.

UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Series: Overdrive Kit/App-Enabled Building and Coding STEM Learning Kit (410 Parts and Connectors), Yellow I really like the JIMU robots, because they're interesting to build, robust when completed, and easy to drive (using the free iOS or Android app). This UBTECH JIMU ROBOTS BUILDERBOTS SERIES OVERDRIVE KIT (410 Parts and Connectors) has everything you need to build a dump-truck robot (Dirtbot) or a dirt-mover robot (Dozerbot). It's a great kit for people (like me) who love building models of heavy construction equipment.

If you want, you can build one model, take it apart, and build the other model. However, be warned that the components are extremely hard to take apart. The components are completely interchangeable with the components in other JIMU robot sets. (The components are NOT compatible with LEGO Technic elements.) Combining JIMU sets gives you more flexibility if you want to create your own robots.

JIMU robots are controlled with Bluetooth--pairing is easy, once they're turned on or plugged into a power source. They don't have separate controllers, so you need a tablet or smartphone to work them. It’s a good idea to charge the controller cubes before you start building--charging takes about an hour--so that you can play with the robot as soon as you're finished building it.

Building instructions are NOT included in the box, except for a Quickstart guide that tells you where to get the detailed instructions. You have to download the JIMU app to get the building instructions. The detailed instructions are presented in 3D--at each step you can rotate the model 360 degrees and look at it from every angle until you’re sure that you’ve got it right.

The JIMU robots are moderately difficult to build, but older kids should be able to complete them. Once the robots are complete, you can use the Blockly coding system to program robotic moves beyond the models’ basic built-in moves. Blockly is part of the downloaded JIMU app.
text_fidelity_b: UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Series: Overdrive Kit/App-Enabled Building and Coding STEM Learning Kit (410 Parts and Connectors), Yellow

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots We've only had this a few days so far, but my kids love it so far! They and their neighborhood friends were playing almost non-stop this entire weekend. It's a pretty unique concept and not at all what I expected coming from the original battleship: Rather than the game of strategy (and sometimes just luck!) that the traditional battleship is, this is mostly a game of skill. There is still some strategy in how you align your boats, but rather than try to determine where the other player's position is, you can see their board and have to toss one of the included ping-pong balls into the holes. Land a ball in all the boat's places, and you've sunk their ship! It is definitely reminiscent of beer pong in skillset, or perhaps one of those arcade games that require you to land a ball in a colored cup. You definitely need more space to play since there will be balls bouncing around if/when you miss, but it is a lot of fun. A creative twist on a classic game!
One thing that is a little strange to me however, is the advertising. The listing for this product says "Nostalgic tabletop gameplay meets interactive digital content for an immersive gaming experience". There's nothing digital about this, let alone interactive digital and immersive. It's a pretty fun analog pick-up-and-play game, which is what I like about it actually, but it was hard to determine what we were getting before we tried it.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots

text_fidelity_a:
Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This game hits that sweet spot where the complexity is enough for adults but not so high that kids struggle. And it’s FUN! It says 9 and up but my 7-year-old caught on pretty quickly and was delighted when we talked about it in terms of executing a program. My family loves this game. My husband and I can see playing it with just adults too.

The gameplay involves drafting cards and then using them to create a plan for how the mole will move on the grid, which is essentially a simple program much like one would write on a computer. It takes some strategy, but you can only predict other people so much and this is where the game shines.

I was worried it would be too complex or long when we read the rules, but it plays very smoothly! We felt comfortable within 2 rounds, and it was a lot of fun seeing how the plans we made would be thwarted as other players move. We also enjoyed how the turn order changed. There are many levels of subtle strategy, I feel like we will be learning new things each time we play. There is a random element of dice when placing a rock on the board, simple but genius game design. It keeps it from feeling unfair, and adds an element of luck to using it.

Even when you are losing, it’s so interesting to see the programs unfold as each card flips that it didn’t feel upsetting, and most of the points are earned in the later rounds as the mounds get higher so you can easily catch back up to an early lead or after a bad round. This means you don’t feel too discouraged if you have a poor start.

I like that it has a defined timeline, there are 6 rounds and you know what they will look like. Overall a great choice for a family game night as it is not likely to overrun an hour.

The double-layer boards and gameplay are unique and the story of the moles is full of flavor. The art is charming and the explanation of the rules such as “moles are too polite so they don’t move when they hit another” is a really sweet touch. The printing is great quality, the game is just beautiful to look at. The box is well-organized making setup and takedown easy, and it looks pretty on the shelf. Plus, we love the moles! The standees make great pieces. This game shows a lot of care in the details, and we love games with a lot of artistic flavor.

We play a lot of games as a family, but when we finished this one kiddo said this was their new favorite! The only downside is the limit of 2-4 players–it keeps it moving but means we can’t invite more friends to play at a time!

Bonus, the box art is beautiful so this also would make a lovely gift to open.
text_fidelity_b: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+

My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set Both of our grandsons really enjoyed this educational toy.

Grandpa had a good time assembling the tracks. Little bit of trial and error, and many pieces look similar. Think of a crossword puzzle. Grandma gave up. Grandma had the track supports in the middle of the track. Not good. Grandpa had the track supports in the air, not on the ground in the first attempt. Not good. Grandpa missed on the first two tries. This was not frustrating but a wonderful experience showing our toddlers how to figure things out. They were impressed with Grandpa. Now they love to assemble the tracks on their own.

Definitely a good educational toy.
The pieces are high quality and fit together very well. They will not come apart by accident.
The photos show how intently our 2 year old grandson is working on putting the tracks together. A big plus.
The carrying case is excellent, and not the usual throw away case. We have had other sets with cases, but they were flimsy, and came apart too easily. The pieces got lost, and we threw them out. All of the pieces fit back in, and our oldest toddler packed everything back by himself.

Because the tracks lock together so well, you could actually lift the tracks off the floor, when finished, and put them away in one or 2 pieces. However, the fun in putting the tracks together, make it worthwhile to take them apart, and place them in the carrying case.

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Artist Studio 24 Glitter Shakers A couple years back, I paid quadruple the amount of money for a Martha Stewart set of glitter that is essentially the same product as this kit. The quality is outstanding. There are large square pieces of glitter with extremely vibrant color, long skinny pieces of glitter that really sparkle and catch the light, little colored glitters that are less glittery and more just a rich "sand" infused with color, and some very fine glitter that is also highly colored.

My nearly 3-year-old son was absolutely enchanted from the beginning about the very concept of glitter, how gorgeous it is, how you get to sprinkle and shake it and it's kind of messy, and I foresee this being an excellent addition to our art projects. I initially thought that this would only be good for children's art projects because I did not expect much of the quality, but the quality level is, as far as I can tell, equivalent to the grown-up stuff you can buy at craft stores like Michael's. Don't tell Martha, but this stuff is just as good.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Artist Studio 24 Glitter Shakers
